title: Request-body limits trust Content-Length and several error/input boundaries are insufficiently defensive

original_titles.title: Phase-1 gaps: Content-Length-only body cap, no content-type check, no IP-level rate limit, unvalidated path IDs yield 500
Body-size limit trusts Content-Length only; malformed value yields 500 and chunked bodies skip the check
Body-size limit only enforced when Content-Length is present
Upload/body size checks trust Content-Length and read-before-check
Body cap 512 KiB vs spec 1 MiB; 2 MiB response cap not enforced
Negative limit query params bypass result caps
Expected database failures surface as 500 INTERNAL_ERROR instead of 503
Unhandled API exceptions and job failures leave no server-side log

problem: The main middleware rejects oversized requests only when Content-Length is present. Chunked/missing length bodies are not streamed through a byte counter, malformed Content-Length conversion can throw, and several endpoints rely on raw dict parsing or unchecked numeric limits. Unexpected API exceptions are returned generically but are not logged with structured diagnostic context.
impact: Large chunked requests can bypass the early cap, invalid inputs can become 500s, negative query limits may disable intended bounds, and operators may not have a request-correlated error trace.

evidence_paths: backend/app/routers/admin.py: raw dict bodies and limit queries
verification.basis: Current source inspection at the main-branch commit listed in metadata. Original audit line numbers are treated as historical and were not reused as current line references.

implementation_steps.action: Implement an ASGI receive wrapper that counts actual bytes as the request body streams; enforce separate limits for JSON, multipart upload and artifact extraction regardless of Content-Length.
Validate Content-Length as a non-negative integer and reject malformed values with 400/413, never a generic 500. Enforce Content-Type and supported encodings.
Constrain every limit/offset/page parameter with lower and upper bounds; use parameterized SQL and reject negative values.
Replace remaining raw dict bodies with strict Pydantic request models and validate UUIDs, numeric ranges, file paths, spans, list sizes and string lengths.
Log unhandled exceptions with request_id, route, safe principal id/role and error class; never include passwords, tokens, challenge content or raw submissions.

acceptance_criteria: Chunked and Content-Length requests are subject to identical body caps.
Malformed headers and negative query values return deterministic 4xx errors.
Every unhandled 500 has a structured request-correlated server log with secrets redacted.
regression_tests: Add a focused failing test before implementation where practical.
Add a negative authorization / boundary test, not only a happy-path test.
Run the affected backend/frontend suite and the full CI workflow before merge.
